report:
## Conclusion

The evidence supports the answer "no" — ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19. The best-quality, largest randomized controlled trials show no meaningful mortality benefit.

**Key evidence:**

1. **ACTIV-6 trial** (NIH-funded, US, >4,000 participants, published in JAMA 2022): This large, rigorous double-blind RCT found ivermectin provided no benefit for recovery time, hospitalization, or other clinical outcomes compared to placebo in outpatients with COVID-19 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic).

2. **TOGETHER trial** (Brazil, NEJM 2022) — described by NEJM itself as "the largest randomized, double-blind trial yet conducted" on ivermectin for COVID-19: It found ivermectin did not reduce the risk of hospitalization or death among high-risk outpatients (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115869). Reporting on this trial by the *New York Times* confirmed "Ivermectin Does Not Reduce Risk of Covid Hospitalization" (https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/30/health/covid-ivermectin-hospitalization.html).

3. A synthesis of major RCTs and updated meta-analyses concludes that "the higher-quality, larger trials and updated meta-analyses find no convincing benefit on mortality, hospitalization, or major clinical endpoints" (https://factually.co/fact-checks/health/ivermectin-covid-19-randomized-trials-meta-analyses-efficacy-safety-limitations-87d1c4).

**Why some sources disagree:** Early, smaller, and lower-quality studies (some later retracted or found fraudulent) suggested large mortality benefits, and these still circulate in advocacy meta-analyses (e.g., c19early.org). However, regulatory bodies including the FDA and WHO advise ivermectin only be used for COVID-19 within clinical trials, reflecting the weight of high-quality evidence showing no mortality benefit.

**Bottom line:** The best available evidence — large, well-designed RCTs (ACTIV-6, TOGETHER) — indicates ivermectin does not reduce COVID-19 mortality.
